title: Two loops, one pump
question: How does blood pick up oxygen and then deliver it?
hook: Blood never leaves its pipes, yet it reaches every corner of the body.
idea: Blood runs two loops from the heart: one to the lungs to take on oxygen and one to the rest of the body to deliver it.

beats.prompt: put these stages of a blood cell's trip in order
items: Oxygen-poor blood enters the right atrium from the venae cavae
The right ventricle pumps it toward the lungs
It takes on oxygen in the lungs and returns to the left atrium
The left side pumps it out through the aorta to the body
beats.explain: Blood enters the right atrium, is pumped to the lungs, comes back oxygen-rich to the left atrium, and is pumped through the aorta into the systemic circulation.

beats.prompt: sort each description into the circuit it belongs to
items: Takes blood from the right heart to the lungs
Returns oxygenated blood to the left heart
Delivers oxygenated blood from the left heart to the rest of the body
Returns blood to the right heart via the venae cavae
beats.explain: The pulmonary circuit links the heart and lungs, while the systemic circuit links the heart and everything else.

beats.prompt: An arthropod's heart pumps hemolymph out into its body. Where does the fluid return?

choices.label: Back through blood vessels, as in a vertebrate
choices.feedback: That is how closed systems like ours work, with blood never leaving the vessels, but arthropods differ.

choices.label: It never returns to the heart
choices.feedback: The heart pumps it out and it does come back, just not through vessels.

beats.explain: Many invertebrates such as arthropods have an open circulatory system, with hemolymph returning via the body cavity rather than via blood vessels.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Vertebrate blood never leaves the network of vessels, so its circulation is closed.
The lymphatic system is a subsystem of the circulatory system.
So the lymphatic system must also be a closed system, like blood circulation.
So lymph is returned to the blood circulation after draining fluid from tissues.
beats.explain: Unlike the closed blood circulatory system, the lymphatic system is an open system.
